next_quarter_outlook.topic: FY28 dark-store expansion upgrade
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management confirms a more aggressive store-addition target with a higher FY28 run-rate than FY27; most new stores will be in smaller cities where paybacks are performing well.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "On the quick commerce business, the new store addition targets that you've laid out are more aggressive than they have been in the past and imply a higher run rate of store additions in FY28 versus FY27." ... "That's right, Garima. Directionally, we've also mentioned in the letter that the bulk of the expansion of these new stores will be in smaller cities. We do expect that to be the focus from here on, and we are seeing great outcomes in terms of payback on these stores in these markets that we've expanded into in the last few quarters."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Akshant Goyal
next_quarter_outlook.location: Transcript pages 2–3 (PDF pages 3–4); analyst question followed by management confirmation

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Blinkit growth acceleration from December
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management explicitly says Blinkit NOV growth should accelerate year-on-year beginning in the December quarter.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "And just to push on that, you're talking about NOV growth pickup starting the December quarter on a YoY basis?" ... "That's right."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Akshant Goyal
next_quarter_outlook.location: Transcript page 7 (PDF page 8); analyst clarification confirmed by management

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Blinkit margins
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Accelerating store additions from OND are not expected to reduce margins in the short term; management expects longer-term expansion.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "No, it was a specific comment. What we are saying here is that as we accelerate store addition, which is starting OND, we don't expect that to hit the margins in the short term. Longer term, of course, margins will continue expanding, but we don't expect that there should be a short-term margin reduction on account of accelerated store addition."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Akshant Goyal

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Blinkit store productivity
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management still sees steady-state NOV per store rising toward about ₹11 lakh per day from ₹9 lakh, though rapid store additions may make the quarterly path uneven.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Basis what we know today, yes, we think NOV per day should go up. We gave guidance last time that in steady state it could get to about INR 11 lakh per day per store. We are at INR 9 lakh today. We do think it will go up directionally over time, but there could be some quarters where the growth in the number of stores is lumpy, and therefore it may not be linearly upwards."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Akshant Goyal

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Food-delivery reinvestment
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Food-delivery margins are expected to stay broadly flat for one to two years as operating leverage is reinvested to expand the market and absolute adjusted EBITDA.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Directionally, we want to maintain margins broadly and reinvest in growth as much as it makes sense to continue to drive the growth upwards. That's what the operating principle is. It's hard to project or comment on margin trajectory every quarter but broadly, over the next 1 or 2 years, we expect the margins to remain flattish."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Akshant Goyal

next_quarter_outlook.topic: dark.ai launch and economics
next_quarter_outlook.summary: dark.ai is a few months from launch; the base case is a high-gross-margin, largely self-funded business that could reach profitability relatively quickly, while the next 12 months should reveal whether it becomes meaningful.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "As a base case, we think this could be a high gross margin business, which could fund itself largely and get to profitability pretty soon. That's the outlook right now. It's very early." ... "We expect the next 12 months to tell us whether any of this will become meaningful."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Akshant Goyal

analyst_focus.topic: How aggressive can Blinkit expansion become without hurting returns?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts repeatedly asked about the upgraded FY28 store plan, smaller-city paybacks, capex per store, competitive visibility, NOV per store and whether accelerated additions would pressure margins.

analyst_focus.topic: Where will growth and margins settle across food delivery and Blinkit?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts pressed on December-quarter Blinkit NOV acceleration, the FY29 adjusted-EBITDA target, food-delivery growth, reinvestment and the durability of margin expansion.

key_risks: A faster dark-store rollout can make store productivity and cash deployment uneven across quarters.
Food-delivery operating leverage is being reinvested, keeping percentage margins broadly flat for one to two years.

evidence.speaker: Garima Mishra and Akshant Goyal

There will be furloughs that will impact the H2, there will be lower working day s and all of those implications and all of those impacts. So that will definitely be there. And like always, we do not have one model that leads to guidance. There are always multiple models that leads to mult iple points of the guidance. At the lower end of the guidance, we have baked in higher uncertainty at the upper end of the guidance, we have baked in an improvement in the environment. next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Nidhu Saxena

next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Nidhu Saxena

analyst_focus.topic: Minimum wages and delivery-centre footprint
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Karnataka and Telangana wage hikes hit margins; analysts asked whether a stay creates upside and why the delivery-centre count and lease assets fell (answer: site consolidation and counting change).

analyst_focus.topic: Will easing payer medical costs reduce cost pressure on vendors?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Payer margins improved in H1 2026; analysts asked if that gives Sagility pricing relief, and management said cost take-out pressure persists.

analyst_focus.topic: What is in the $40 million ACV and what M&A comes next?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts sought payer versus provider mix, deal duration and margins, and remaining capability gaps for further acquisitions; the segment split was not available.

analyst_focus.topic: What does the low double-digit guidance include?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Clarified that guidance is organic only, with CareSeed and Chirok additive.

key_risks: Open enrolment and AEP revenue is expected flat to slightly lower year on year, pressuring the seasonal peak.
Margin upgrade assumes FX stays at current levels and efficiency gains persist.
AI-driven productivity gains are largely passed through to clients, capping structural margin upside and keeping client cost pressure high.
Provider organic revenue has been weak (discrete project taper at one client) and Chirok was acquired only a day before the call, so integration and AI disruption of coding are open risks.
Karnataka and Telangana minimum-wage increases are in guidance; a reversal is upside but the current impact is a cost headwind.

material_guidance_changes.magnitude: Both ends of the range raised by 100 bps
material_guidance_changes.explicit_statement: Management states it is raising FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance from 24-25% to 25-26%.

evidence.speaker: Ramesh Gopalan
evidence.quote: "we are raising our FY '27 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance from our earlier 24% to 25% to a new 25% to 26%."

AXISBANK.description: Company-website transcript linked from the NSE covering letter (user-approved source exception).

next_quarter_outlook.topic: NIM uplift expected from Q3 as FCNR(B) funds retire costly NRTDs
next_quarter_outlook.summary: The 11 bps FCNR(B) drag was a one-quarter optics effect; part of the funds already retired expensive non-resident term deposits late in Q2, so Q3 should see NIM benefit, while the through-cycle 3.8% NIM guidance is unchanged.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So we should be able to see some benefit of that come through in the next quarter in terms of NIM uplift."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Rajeev Mantri

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Q3 and Q4 to show NIM benefit from balance-sheet optimisation
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Redeploying FCNR(B) funds into loans and retiring higher-cost liabilities is expected to lift NIM over the next two quarters.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "I think in Q3 and Q4, you should be able to see some sort of a benefit coming through due to the optimization exercise that we'll be doing."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Rajeev Mantri

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Sequential NIM improvement intended, but no firm timeline
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management wants NIM to move up each quarter via asset mix, liability mix and rate hikes, with some headwinds, and declines to call a time frame.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "But sequentially, we should be able to show an improvement going forward."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Rajeev Mantri

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Card fee weakness partly a festive-timing shift into October
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Year-on-year fee growth was weak because the festive spend month moved from September last year to October this year, implying some catch-up in Q3.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "last year, September was when the festive month had started. This year, that has shifted to October. So, there is a bit of a temporal difference on account of that."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Subrat Mohanty

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Latest repo-rate increase flows through loan yields in Q4, not Q3
next_quarter_outlook.summary: The bank reprices its repo-linked book in the last week of the quarter, so the book-wide benefit of the latest repo hike lands in Q4; only new repo-linked loans reprice sooner.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So the latest repo rate increase from a book stock perspective, the benefit we will actually see in Q4 as opposed to in Q3."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Rajeev Mantri

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Credit costs expected to improve further, no numeric guidance
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Slippage ratios and recoveries are improving in individual portfolios; part of the improvement is mix-driven, and the bank will not guide a credit cost number.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "But directionally, what I can confirm is that we are on the trajectory towards improvement. I think there is some further improvement that also we can expect."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Rajeev Mantri

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Bancassurance: draft IRDA commission rules likely 6-9 months away
next_quarter_outlook.summary: The bank expects regulation to take time, possibly with a glide path, and plans to mitigate through volumes, product mix and other fee sources; it will not quantify the impact.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So, I think we might get about 6 to 9 months before that comes through. So, we'll try and mitigate the impact during that point of time."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Subrat Mohanty

next_quarter_outlook.topic: FCNR(B) liquidity not fully deployed, leaving growth runway
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Part of the incremental FCNR(B) liability is still unused for asset growth while LCR is held in a 115-120% band, so loan growth can run ahead of deposit raising in coming quarters.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "we have not used the full FCNR (B) liquidity to grow our assets, right? So to that extent, there is runway for the balance sheet to grow"
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Neeraj Gambhir

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Labour-code costs may recur if new guidelines arrive
next_quarter_outlook.summary: The Q2 one-offs included labour-code provisions on outsourced staff and ESIC; management says known items are covered but the area is evolving.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So far, based on what we have been aware of, we have already taken those into accounts. But this is an area where, you know, some new guidelines, etcetera, whenever they come, we will have to deal with that."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Rajeev Mantri

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Second-half posture: watchful on geopolitics, inflation, tariffs and weather
next_quarter_outlook.summary: CEO flags West Asia tensions, commodity prices and weather risks while expressing confidence in sustainable and profitable growth.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "As we enter second half of the year, we continue to remain watchful and closely monitor the evolving external environment."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Amitabh Chaudhry

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Through-cycle NIM target of 3.8% unchanged, no timeline given
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management will not say how long it takes to get to 3.8% from 3.36% (3.47% ex-FCNR).
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Though structurally, we are working towards our through-cycle guidance of 3.8% that we have mentioned earlier."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Rajeev Mantri

next_quarter_outlook.topic: ECL transition: no material impact expected, backed by ~INR 8,000 cr contingent provisions
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Both the transition and the subsequent flow are expected to be non-material for FY28, with floor rates for stage 1 and 2 still being worked through.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "we don't expect any material impact to come through on the transition itself. This is also supported because we have existing contingent provisions almost close to 8,000 crores that continue"
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Rajeev Mantri

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Loan growth guided at 300 bps above industry over the medium term
next_quarter_outlook.summary: The medium-term growth guidance is reiterated as the base for NII; no specific NII number is given.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "We have guided for 300 basis points higher than the industry average over the medium term."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Rajeev Mantri

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Retail share of loans to be rebuilt towards above 55%
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Corporate has outgrown retail; management says it is working to stop the retail mix slipping further and to return above 55% as retail book growth catches up with disbursements.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "we get back to the above 55% retail mix. So that effort is on at this point in time."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Subrat Mohanty

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Corporate lending growth described as diversified and sustainable
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Growth is spread across capex, project finance, refinancing and working capital with selective origination; downstream salary and liability benefits are cited.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So corporate growth is sustainable because it's well diversified across sector segments and financing categories."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Vijay Mulbagal
next_quarter_outlook.role: Bank executive (role not stated in transcript)

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Cost-to-assets expected to keep falling once one-offs fall away
next_quarter_outlook.summary: The Q2 cost-to-assets uptick on a quarterly basis is attributed to one-timers (labour code and FCNR costs); management expects the ratio to fall further adjusted for these.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "I think this is primarily due to the one-timers that we have seen in the cost for this quarter. That's why I think, adjusted for that, you will see the ratio coming down even further."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Rajeev Mantri

next_quarter_outlook.topic: UPI MDR revenue upside cannot be sized; implementation postponed
next_quarter_outlook.summary: The bank plays across issuing, PSP and acquiring roles but gives no revenue guidance and may reinvest part of any MDR revenue into the ecosystem.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "at this stage, we can't give any specific guidance because the MDR implementation has been postponed."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Arnika Dixit
next_quarter_outlook.role: Bank executive (role not stated in transcript)

next_quarter_outlook.topic: No equity capital needed for growth or protection
next_quarter_outlook.summary: CET1 at 14.61% plus ~49 bps of unreckoned provision buffer; management rules out equity raising.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "We reiterate that we do not need equity capital for either the growth or protection pillars."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Rajeev Mantri

analyst_focus.topic: Has NIM bottomed, and what is the exit rate and path from here?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Five analysts pressed on NIM: reported 3.36% was down 37 bps YoY with an 11 bps FCNR(B) distortion. They tested whether Q2 is the trough, the September exit NIM, how the FCNR drag unwinds, and the Q4 timing of repo-hike repricing; management declined monthly NIM and a firm timeline.

analyst_focus.topic: Will corporate keep out-growing retail, and is that growth durable?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Retail share fell below the previously signalled 55% as wholesale grew 34% YoY; analysts asked if the mix would keep shifting given wide AA spreads and industry-wide FCNR-funded corporate lending.

analyst_focus.topic: Where do credit costs settle, including ECL and FY28?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Net credit cost fell to 0.45% after standard-asset provisions on FCNR loans; analysts asked about normalisation versus further improvement, unusual recoveries, and whether the ECL transition removes the ROA tailwind from lower credit costs in FY28.

analyst_focus.topic: Why is fee growth weak and what do regulatory changes do to it?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Fee grew only 6% YoY on cards, payments and asset-linked fee dilution; analysts asked about the draft IRDA bancassurance guidelines, how to offset them, the UPI MDR opportunity and any fee on FCNR mobilisation (none charged).

analyst_focus.topic: Is operating leverage real once one-offs are stripped out?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Opex rose 11% QoQ and cost-to-assets looked higher on a quarterly basis; analysts asked about the INR 254 cr one-offs (labour code, FCNR) and whether further jaws are available.

analyst_focus.topic: Has the FCNR(B) money been fully deployed, and what does that mean for liquidity?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: A back-of-envelope check showed INR 1 trillion raised against INR 80,000 cr net deposit growth and INR 68,000 cr loan growth with LCR flat near 119%; analysts asked how much room is left to grow and why run-off rates rose.

analyst_focus.topic: Personal loan strategy and unsecured growth
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: With peers growing PL faster, an analyst asked whether the bank would extend PL beyond salaried borrowers; management said PL stays salaried-only and self-employed borrowers go through business loans.

analyst_focus.topic: How will NII momentum evolve?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: NII growth accelerated to 5% QoQ; analysts asked whether the rate hike and FCNR deployment will extend it; no NII guidance was given.

analyst_focus.topic: ECLGS disbursement scale
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts sized the government-guaranteed emergency line exposure: around 12,500 loans for INR 10,700 cr sanctioned, about 80% disbursed.

key_risks: Management will not give a timeline for NIM recovery to 3.8% and NIM still depends on FCNR(B) deployment and mix.
Fee growth is weak (6% YoY); draft IRDA bancassurance rules and uncertain UPI MDR add regulatory fee risk.
Retail share of loans has slipped below the 55% level management still wants to return to.
Labour-code related expense is described as an evolving area that could produce further one-offs.
Geopolitical tension in West Asia, commodity inflation, tariffs and weather risks are explicitly flagged for the second half.

TORNTPHARM.description: Company-website transcript linked from the NSE covering letter (user-approved source exception).

next_quarter_outlook.topic: JB margin improvement to continue for the next two to three quarters
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Q1-to-Q2 JB margin gains came mainly from field-force merger savings; the same run-rate of improvement is expected to continue.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So, I would expect quarter-on-quarter, this same run rate of improvement can continue maybe for the next two, three quarters."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Aman Mehta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Germany: best case is a slight decline in coming quarters, stability after 3-4 quarters
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Loss of tenders, third-party supply disruption and government-mandated price cuts have hit the non-retail business; management declines to guide.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Best case, I would say slight decline in the coming quarters, and eventually some stability after maybe 3 or 4 quarters."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Sanjay Gupta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: INR 950-960 cr second tranche of the Novartis ophthalmology deal due in December
next_quarter_outlook.summary: A pending cash payment on the JB-Novartis ophthalmology portfolio is expected in the December quarter, which matters for net-debt trajectory (net debt/EBITDA now 1.8x).
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "there is a second tranche of payment of about INR950 crores, INR960 crores that is pending. Would that be due anytime soon? ... That would be in December of this year."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Bino (Elara Capital); Aman Mehta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: JB India branded business to re-accelerate above 10% in H2
next_quarter_outlook.summary: After 13% in Q1 and 7% in Q2 (integration-hit), management expects gradual quarterly recovery and H2 JB India growth above the H1 average of 10%.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "if H1 is at 10% growth for the India branded business, I would expect that H2 should be perhaps higher than that."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Aman Mehta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Overall JB growth back to double digit in H2; international recovery slower
next_quarter_outlook.summary: JB international was down 7% in Q2 on plant-network and QC integration delays; management says the recovery may take longer but total JB should still return to double-digit growth in H2.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So while the actions have been taken, the recovery may take slightly longer in the international business, but overall we still feel that in H2, the overall JB growth should be double-digit."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Aman Mehta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Group EBITDA margin to be a little above 33.5% in H2
next_quarter_outlook.summary: No numeric guidance, but management expects the second half to improve on Q2's 33.5%, with JB margins rising gradually for two to three more quarters.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So, I think there should be a gradual increase in the EBITDA margin. But I think we're not guiding on the number part, but at least definitely we feel H2 should be little higher than 33.5%."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Sudhir Menon

next_quarter_outlook.topic: US: four to five more filings this fiscal; price erosion rises in H2 from new competitors
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Filings of 9-10 products in the year will exceed several prior years, but management expects new competition on recent launches to raise pricing pressure in H2.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "we think we can file four to five at least more before this fiscal year ends. ... I expect some new competitors on our recent launches in H2."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Sanjay Gupta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Indian pharma market growth of at least 10% to persist through next financial year
next_quarter_outlook.summary: H1 market growth was about 12%; management sees it holding for the rest of this year and slipping only 1-2 points next year, calling this year potentially a one-off.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "We think this market growth is likely to sustain for the rest of the year, and perhaps from next year it may drop a little bit, say 1%, 2%, but minimum 10% is what we think should continue from here on as well, at least for the next financial year."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Aman Mehta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Curatio to sustain high growth for the rest of the year and likely a couple of years
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Curatio grew 34% in Q2 and H1 and is now 7-8% of base India; management cannot say 30% growth lasts 3-5 years but sees the trend continuing.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "I think it should be possible to sustain high growth for at least a couple of years."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Aman Mehta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Brazil expected to keep growing mid-teens; Brazil generic semaglutide launch in 6-9 months
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Four business units are performing; 53 molecules await ANVISA approval over about three years; a first local generic semaglutide launch has expanded the market.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Brazil, we are optimistic, it'll continue to grow double-digit, mid-teens or something in that range"
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Sanjay Gupta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Field force held at 9,100 this year; possible 500 addition, 9,500-9,600 next year
next_quarter_outlook.summary: No headcount change this fiscal year after the field-force merger, with a possible base-business expansion later.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "We expect potentially some expansion may be required in the base business, so say maybe by 500 MRs or so. But we're not fully certain on what the next year's picture looks like, but it could be say something between 9,500 to 9,600."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Aman Mehta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: INR 450 cr cost synergies now targeted in two years rather than three
next_quarter_outlook.summary: About half of the synergy is already in this year's margins and most comes through by next year; the INR 450 cr quantum is held and any upside will be reviewed in a couple of quarters.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "But directionally, yes, we've been able to achieve that much faster. Instead of three years, I think we should be able to get there in two years' time."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Aman Mehta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: India revenue synergies to start showing next year
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Cross-selling and adding JB brands to Torrent divisions typically take 6-12 months, with international synergies a longer 2-3 year journey.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So, I think next year should see a reasonable improvement in the topline growth through revenue synergies."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Aman Mehta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: No FY28 margin guidance until Q1 FY28
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management will wait for a full-year combined base before guiding FY28 EBITDA margins.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "No, we are not giving any guidance for FY28. We are just waiting for the full-year base to come in, and then probably next year quarter one, we will guide it."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Sudhir Menon

next_quarter_outlook.topic: R&D to stay at 4-4.5% of revenue for the next couple of years
next_quarter_outlook.summary: R&D is stepping up to lift US ANDA filings from low to high single digits a year; the Q2 increase is expected to persist, which caps margin expansion.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "We believe that the range should not exceed, say, between 4% to 4.5% even in the following year."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Aman Mehta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: India semaglutide: lost share to be recovered; generic market could reach INR 2,000-2,500 cr in 3-5 years
next_quarter_outlook.summary: After a roughly two-month injectable supply gap, supplies were fully restored in September; the analyst's estimate of a INR 2,000-2,500 cr market over three to five years was called 'not out of range'.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Yes. That that should be possible. At least three to five years, that number is not out of range."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Aman Mehta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: India semaglutide pricing expected stable to gradually higher
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Because the products are branded, management expects no per-patient price erosion despite rising competition.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "And in fact, the price would only be stable or gradually increase over the next couple of years."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Aman Mehta

analyst_focus.topic: How fast does JB recover, in India and internationally?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: JB revenue was flat YoY after integration; analysts asked whether the flat trend persists and whether international disruptions take longer to fix. Answer: India recovers gradually above 10% in H2; international slower; total double-digit in H2.

analyst_focus.topic: Are INR 450 cr cost synergies conservative, and when do revenue synergies come?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Roughly half appears already in margins; Neha Manpuria, Damayanti Kerai and Kunal Dhamesha tested upside, timing (two years versus three), and when revenue synergies start; management held the INR 450 cr number.

analyst_focus.topic: Where do group and JB EBITDA margins go from 33.5%?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Margin fell slightly QoQ (33.8% to 33.5%) as R&D rose 0.7 pts of revenue; analysts asked for JB margin parity with Torrent India, the sequential JB gain and FY28-29 direction; management gave only directional H2 'a little higher' commentary.

analyst_focus.topic: Where will the combined India field force settle?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: The 9,100 MR count after merging divisions affects cost and productivity; management said flat this year with a possible 500 addition.

analyst_focus.topic: Is the higher R&D and US filing push sustainable and productive?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: R&D at 4.2% of revenue was above Q1's 3.5%; analysts asked about new investment avenues and US filing cadence, and whether US growth is durable versus price erosion.

analyst_focus.topic: How big and how profitable is India semaglutide, and what about Brazil?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Torrent holds 32% share after a supply gap; analysts asked about market size, pricing per patient and Brazil launch timing, which are key new profit pools.

analyst_focus.topic: Why is Indian pharma market growth suddenly 12%, and will it last?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Market growth is well above recent years; analysts probed GLP-1, trade generics and consolidation as causes. Management could not pinpoint the delta but sees at least 10% next year.

analyst_focus.topic: Is US growth from launches durable?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: US constant-currency revenue grew 13%; analysts asked how much comes from products with durable advantage. Management said there is no durable advantage in generics; the base is flat and growth comes from new launches.

analyst_focus.topic: Brazil growth drivers and constraints
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Growth was split about equally across price, volume and launches; analysts asked about 53 pending approvals, the constraint (ANVISA timing and local competition) and growth outlook.

analyst_focus.topic: Germany outlook
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Revenue fell about 13% in constant currency; management could offer only a best case of slight decline for coming quarters.

analyst_focus.topic: Curatio and OTC scale-up
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Curatio is now 7-8% of base India and growing 34%; analysts asked about sustainability and new OTC launches, which are mostly brand extensions.

analyst_focus.topic: JB-Novartis ophthalmology deal risk and payment timing
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: An analyst asked whether Novartis India changes endanger the deal and when the INR 950-960 cr balance is due; management said the contract is clear and payment is in December.

key_risks: JB international recovery is slower than India and depends on plant-network and QC integration milestones.
R&D at 4-4.5% of revenue for two to three years limits margin expansion even as synergies come through.
New competitors on recent US launches are expected to raise price erosion in H2.
Germany remains weak, with only a best-case outlook of slight decline.
India semaglutide faces rising competition; Q2 shows how supply interruptions can cost share.
A INR 950-960 cr Novartis ophthalmology payment is due in December.

material_guidance_changes.new_guidance: INR 450 cr in about two years
material_guidance_changes.magnitude: Same quantum delivered one year earlier; further upside deferred for a couple of quarters
material_guidance_changes.explicit_statement: Management says synergies are being achieved much faster than planned, in two years instead of three.

evidence.speaker: Aman Mehta
evidence.quote: "But directionally, yes, we've been able to achieve that much faster. Instead of three years, I think we should be able to get there in two years' time."

OBEROIRLTY.description: Company-website transcript linked from the NSE covering letter (user-approved source exception).

next_quarter_outlook.topic: H2 launch pipeline likely to slip by a quarter here and there
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Planned launches (Aurelius at Peddar Road, Thane Tower A, Jardin, Forestville tower, Alibaug, Mulund and Sky City commercial, Ralli Wolf in Mulund) are expected to shift out modestly.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "we had a bunch of projects that we were originally wanting to launch. So probably they'll just slide over a quarter here and there."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Vikas Oberoi

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Ritz-Carlton hotel commissioning around Q1 next year
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Roughly 6-9 months to go for the hotel, adding to the annuity portfolio in early FY28.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Ritz-Carlton, the hotel, when should we expect the commissioning? ... So maybe first quarter next year? Another 6 to 9 months to go."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Murtaza (Kotak Securities); Vikas Oberoi

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Three Sixty North collections spill into the December quarter
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Only about 10% of the 20% due within 90 days was collected in Q2 because the launch was in early July; the balance should be collected next quarter, supporting operating cash flow.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So technically, your 90 days will end in the first week of October. So that's why it will spill over into the next quarter."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Saumil Daru

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Thane prices to rise on input cost increases
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Inventory is ample and sales velocity is improving as buildings top up, but management plans price increases in Thane.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Thane, very clearly, we have enough inventory and you will see a price increase in Thane also in a bit because there is an input cost increase."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Vikas Oberoi

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Gurugram Phase 2 awaits approvals; launch not to be rushed
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management says construction is unrestricted despite litigation, Phase 1 is sold out (over INR 8,000 cr of sales), and Phase 2 will start once approvals arrive and the experience centre is ready, which also supports higher pricing.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "second phase we are waiting for some additional approvals on the second phase. And as soon as that comes, we hopefully will be able to start with that."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Vikas Oberoi

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Adarsh Nagar launch delayed by pending clearances
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Design is ready but approvals are taking longer than expected, so a launch this year is not assured.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Like really -- like knocking the door, but it is taking a little longer than what we thought."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Vikas Oberoi

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Construction outflow about INR 1,000 cr for FY27
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Full-year construction cash outflow on ongoing projects is guided at roughly INR 1,000 cr, a small number against Q2's strong NCR collections.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "For the whole year, it will be in the region of about Rs. 1,000-odd crores."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Saumil Daru

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Mulund Ralli Wolf launch price still being debated; Q4 launch not confirmed
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Analyst floated INR 38,000-40,000 per sq ft and a Q4 launch; management did not commit to either.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "We are internally debating, as we speak, what should the price there be."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Vikas Oberoi

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Annuity asset spend spread over about four years (Thane, Borivali office)
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Mall, hotel, club and school at Thane and a 8-10 lakh sq ft Borivali asset will be funded gradually over four years.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Obviously, all of these costs are going to get spread over about 4 years."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Saumil Daru

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Borivali hotel targeted for around end of next calendar year; Thane about four years away
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Annuity growth is back-ended: Borivali hotel is under interiors; Thane has not started.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Borivali, the target is like end of next Calendar Year, I would say, end of next Calendar year, next Diwali and around. And Thane, we are yet to start work there. So that is a good four years away."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Vikas Oberoi

next_quarter_outlook.topic: RLDA project: sell-versus-lease decision still open
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Approvals are in process for an office, small hotel and retail development; management has not decided between selling strata and leasing.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "we haven't really decided whether we will be selling and leasing or only leasing."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Vikas Oberoi

next_quarter_outlook.topic: NCR expansion: open to land for residential and annuity assets across NCR
next_quarter_outlook.summary: After Gurugram, management says it will buy land or do JDAs in Noida, Gurugram and Delhi, including malls and offices; it will not disclose pending deals.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So we are open to buying land for malls or offices even any other annuity assets in NCR."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Vikas Oberoi

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Further Gurugram sales contribution not guided
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management says remaining Gurugram inventory could achieve meaningful sales but explicitly declines forward-looking statements, so FY28 NCR contribution remains unquantified.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Frankly, even if you open our booking and sell the rest of the inventory, we'll easily achieve that. But like I said, we frankly don't give any forward-looking statements."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Vikas Oberoi

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Three Sixty brand in other cities (e.g. south India) possible but undated
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Landowners are offering parcels for Three Sixty-style projects; no commitment on timing.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "No, you never -- you can never count that out ever, but I can't give you a guarantee of when."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Vikas Oberoi

analyst_focus.topic: What do the Gurugram litigation and Phase 2 timing mean for NCR?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Three Sixty North was a very large launch (INR 8,000+ cr of sales); analysts needed to know if construction or Phase 2 is at risk and how much of FY28 sales NCR can contribute. Answer: no construction restriction, Phase 2 awaits approvals, no forward guidance.

analyst_focus.topic: Which H2 launches will actually happen?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Pre-sales visibility depends on Peddar Road, Thane, Forestville, Mulund and Adarsh Nagar launches; management said several would slip by a quarter and Adarsh Nagar approvals are delayed.

analyst_focus.topic: How do collections and cash margin convert from the NCR launch?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Cash margin hit roughly 80% in Q2 on Three Sixty North collections with no revenue recognition; analysts reconciled the INR 835 cr collected against the 20%-in-90-days milestone and asked for steady-state margins. Management said the balance spills into Q3.

analyst_focus.topic: When do annuity and hotel assets commission?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Annuity growth drives long-term valuation; analysts asked about Ritz-Carlton (Q1 next year), Borivali (end of next calendar year), Thane (about four years), I-Ven Worli (construction started) and RLDA (strategy undecided).

analyst_focus.topic: How is the NCR business development pipeline building?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: With MMR visibility for two to three years, analysts asked which NCR markets and asset types are open and when new large deals close; management declined to disclose negotiations.

analyst_focus.topic: Is luxury demand softening, given sales velocity and pricing at Three Sixty West?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Karan Khanna noted 3 units in YTD FY27 versus 10 in FY26 despite sharp price rises; management said it is project- and floor-specific, not a market signal.

analyst_focus.topic: What will Mulund Ralli Wolf be priced at and when does it launch?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Eternia is up 22% YoY to about INR 36,500 per sq ft; the next launch price and timing are a Q4 pricing catalyst; not decided.

analyst_focus.topic: What is the FY27 construction outflow and annuity capex phasing?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Funding needs for ongoing projects (about INR 1,000 cr this year) and annuity assets (spread over four years) frame free cash flow.

analyst_focus.topic: Why did the balance sheet expand on both sides?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Fair-value accounting of area-based land consideration added to inventory and provisions in the launch quarter; nothing operational.

key_risks: Gurugram matter is sub judice and Phase 2 depends on additional approvals; management declined to comment on litigation.
Several launches (Adarsh Nagar, Peddar Road, Thane, Forestville, Ralli Wolf) face approval or timing slippage.
Management explicitly gives no forward-looking statements on Gurugram or NCR contribution to FY28 sales.
Three Sixty West volumes fell to 3 units YTD versus 10 in FY26, raising questions about luxury demand at higher prices.
Input cost increases in Thane and long gestation of hotels and annuity assets (Thane about four years) delay returns.

FEDERALBNK.description: Company-website transcript linked from the NSE covering letter (user-approved source exception).

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Lending yields bottomed last quarter
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Adjusting for FCNR effects, lending yields were flat to slightly higher QoQ, and management treats Q1 FY27 as the trough of the yield cycle.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So, we have already seen the bottom of that cycle last quarter, I would say."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: KVS Manian

next_quarter_outlook.topic: October repo hike: external-benchmark loans reprice before deposits; deposit competition to rise when liquidity normalises
next_quarter_outlook.summary: The 25 bp hike on 7 October helps near-term margin because the repo-linked book resets quickly while deposits reprice only at maturity, but liquidity normalisation will intensify deposit competition.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "loan book will reprice ahead of deposits, which will reprice as they mature. We also expect competition for deposits to intensify once the liquidity situation normalizes."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Venkatraman V

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Gold-loan yields can rise with rates, capped by PSU competition
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Gold loans are roughly one-year products that reprice on maturity, so management expects to raise pricing as rates rise, but PSU banks charging under 9% limit how far.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "if yields would go up, do you see scope to increase the price? ... Of course, of course. Why would we not?"
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Jai Prakash Mundhra (ICICI Securities); KVS Manian

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Staff-cost picture to be clearer within about a quarter
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Employee cost is rising on hiring and branch openings and carries an actuarial/retirement-cost component that can partly write back as rates rise; an estimate is expected in the next quarter or so.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "But I think we will be in a better position over the next quarter or so to be able to estimate this better."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: KVS Manian

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Loan growth guidance of mid-teens maintained despite ~18% ex-leverage growth
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Even with underlying growth around 18% excluding externally leveraged FCNR loans, management does not raise the mid-teens growth guidance.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "is there any revision in growth guidance? ... We continue to maintain what we had guided: mid-teens as the growth-rate guidance. We continue to maintain that guidance."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Chintan Joshi (Autonomous); KVS Manian

next_quarter_outlook.topic: NIM guidance: 5-6 bps improvement per quarter on average, not linear
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management restates the year's NIM guidance after a flat-to-down-one-bp Q2 (3.32%) and says it is still striving for it.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Broadly, I would say for the year we gave a broad guidance that it will be 5–6 basis points per quarter improvement, and we had said that it will not be linear; it will vary from quarter to quarter, but on an average, we should get that. We are still striving to get that number."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: KVS Manian

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Cost-to-income to be held in a narrow range; no cost benefits to be baked in
next_quarter_outlook.summary: CFO cites about 52% and the CEO a base of about 54%; both say to assume cost-to-income stays around current levels while the bank invests in branches, people, technology and a new sales channel.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "We will continue to operate in the range of 52% on the C/I ratio, as explained in the past as well."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Venkatraman V

next_quarter_outlook.topic: ROA guidance: 3-4 bps improvement a quarter on average
next_quarter_outlook.summary: After a 10 bp jump in Q2 to 1.32%, management sticks with the guided improvement rate and the 1.5% ROA question is answered only with that guidance.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "We have given you guidance on the ROA in the past: three to four basis points per quarter is the improvement we want to strive for."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: KVS Manian

next_quarter_outlook.topic: CASA guidance unchanged
next_quarter_outlook.summary: After CASA grew 6.4% QoQ and 22.6% YoY, the CFO says the CASA guidance is unchanged.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "CASA grew 6.4% QoQ, and there is no change to our guidance on CASA."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Venkatraman V

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Modelling note: ESOP fair-value accounting adds INR 32.7 cr to employee cost
next_quarter_outlook.summary: From April 2026 all ESOPs move to fair-value accounting, cutting PAT by INR 24.5 cr; management calls it a one-time policy change that analysts should model in.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So, when you are modelling employee cost and profitability, please keep this accounting change in mind."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Venkatraman V

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Asset-quality watch: El Nino, geopolitics, rates and inflation; no impact yet
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management has deliberately held back on agriculture and microfinance and sees no portfolio impact so far.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "we continue to watch the outcomes of El Niño, geopolitics, interest-rate scenario, inflation — all of that. Just now, we do not see any impact on our portfolio."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: KVS Manian

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Rate cycle seen as supportive; constructive on remaining quarters
next_quarter_outlook.summary: CEO expects the rising rate cycle to help the NIM trajectory and remains constructive for the rest of FY27.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "The evolving interest rate cycle should provide an additional supportive factor as we move forward."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: KVS Manian

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Opex investment phase continues; do not bake in benefits
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Cost-to-assets above 2.3% is part of a deliberate couple-of-years investment phase.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "we have maintained that: do not bake in benefits on our OPEX, and that guidance remains as of now."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: KVS Manian

next_quarter_outlook.topic: ECL transition impact unchanged at under 2% of net worth
next_quarter_outlook.summary: The expected-credit-loss transition impact is not changed by the rise in G-Sec yields.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "last quarter you had mentioned that the impact is less than 2% of net worth. ... Yes. We talked about the expected credit-loss impact, and that does not change with this."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Jai Prakash Mundhra (ICICI Securities); KVS Manian

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Inorganic growth only if accretive; no comment on the MFI/merger rumours
next_quarter_outlook.summary: CEO sets accretion as the first test for any deal and declined to discuss specific transactions or segments.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Therefore, the first principle is that it should be accretive."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: KVS Manian

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Wealth business for NRI franchise remains a committed priority
next_quarter_outlook.summary: The bank intends to monetise its deep NRI deposit base through wealth products and keeps CASA initiatives ongoing.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "our NRI franchise needs to be holistically covered, and one of the items there was building our wealth business. We remain committed to doing that."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: KVS Manian

analyst_focus.topic: How much did FCNR(B) lift deposits and hurt NIM, and where is the money deployed?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Federal participated in the special FCNR/NRE window with lower leverage than peers; analysts tried to compute NIM ex-FCNR and deployment, and the CEO said NIM was affected but would not quantify.

analyst_focus.topic: Are there acquisition plans (MFI or other), and would they dilute quality?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Press rumours about an MFI deal worried investors given steep credit cycles in microfinance; four analysts raised it and the CEO would only describe principles (accretive, capability or scale).

analyst_focus.topic: Is loan growth sustainable and will guidance be raised?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Growth ex-leverage was about 18% against mid-teens guidance, with strong gold, personal, commercial and card growth.

analyst_focus.topic: Is opex growth consistent with the cost-to-income guidance?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Opex looked high even after ESOP adjustment, with cost-to-assets above 2.3% on branch and hiring spend; analysts asked if the investment phase is temporary.

analyst_focus.topic: How structural is the record fee income?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Fee income rose 22% QoQ to INR 1,167 cr; analysts asked about FCNR-linked fees, base effects after two weak quarters and trading income repeating.

analyst_focus.topic: Have lending yields bottomed and how will margins move after the rate hike?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Yields had been drifting down; analysts wanted to know whether margins improve after the 25 bps hike and whether the 5-6 bps per quarter guidance still holds.

analyst_focus.topic: Gold-loan pricing, LTV and competition
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Gold loans grew 37% YoY with LTV up from about 55% to 60-61% and a new income-generating gold loan product; analysts probed repricing and PSU competition.

analyst_focus.topic: Is asset quality exposed to inflation and El Nino?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: With CPI rising to 5.54% and policy turning to calibrated tightening, analysts asked if high-yield segments show stress; none yet.

analyst_focus.topic: How big is the ECL transition hit?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: G-Sec yields hardened about 40 bps; analysts asked if the under-2%-of-net-worth impact changes.

analyst_focus.topic: What is the path to a 1.5% ROA and what are risk-adjusted margins?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: With asset quality strong and cost investments continuing, ROA upside depends on NIM and fees; management referred to the 3-4 bps per quarter guidance.

analyst_focus.topic: NRI franchise monetisation and CASA initiatives
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: NRI deposits are a core franchise; analysts asked if product depth (wealth) is being built and what drove CASA success over six to eight quarters.

key_risks: Competition for deposits is expected to intensify once system liquidity normalises.
Opex investment phase (branches, people, technology) keeps cost-to-assets elevated and management says not to assume cost benefits.
Gold-loan growth is exposed to PSU price competition below 9% and an LTV that has risen to about 60%.
M&A speculation (including MFI) creates strategy and integration uncertainty that management declined to address.
Inflation, El Nino, geopolitics and rate moves could affect asset quality; management is watchful though no impact is visible yet.
NIM improvement is guided as non-linear, and the quarterly margin was flat after FCNR(B) effects.

RBLBANK.description: Company-website transcript linked from the NSE covering letter (user-approved source exception).

next_quarter_outlook.topic: NIM expected slightly lower in Q3, edging up in Q4
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Q2 NIM of 4.61% benefits from FCNR/equity liquidity parked in short-term investments; a full quarter of FCNR leverage costs and slow deployment point to a dip in Q3, then a rise in Q4 as the repo hike flows through.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "But on the margin, I would imagine that we should be slightly lower next quarter, and then, probably inch up in Q4."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Jaideep Iyer

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Full-quarter FCNR leverage drag offsets repo hike in Q3
next_quarter_outlook.summary: The GIFT City FCNR leverage ran for only about a month and a half in Q2, so Q3 carries the full-quarter cost against a partial repo-hike benefit; improvement then depends on how fast liquidity moves from investments to loans.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "We're fairly confident to say you will see a little bit of reduction in the next quarter just on account of where the mix is sitting right now on the balance sheet."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Bank management (speaker not named in transcript)

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Repo-linked loans reset on a 90-day cycle; full benefit next quarter
next_quarter_outlook.summary: About 58% of the book is externally benchmarked (32% repo-linked) and most loans reset within the quarter, so the October rate increase shows fully in Q3-Q4.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So, the reset is a 90-day reset, so you will expect that most of the loans will get reset by end of the quarter. So, we'll see the full benefit in the next quarter."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Bhavin Lakhpatwala

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Credit-card slippages to fall to about INR 400 cr in Q3-Q4; card credit cost toward 6%
next_quarter_outlook.summary: September monthly slippages were already 125-130 cr against 600+ for the quarter; card credit cost should drop from low double digits to the 6% zone, and cards provisioning of about INR 575 cr should fall.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "we would expect credit card slippages to come down to around a 400 plus-minus number for Q3, Q4 kind of numbers. And therefore, credit costs on cards should come down from the low double digits that we've seen to the 6% zone."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Jaideep Iyer

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Retail slippages expected to trend materially lower, consistent with prior guidance
next_quarter_outlook.summary: JLG microfinance is back to normal, rural collections are stable, and credit-card trends match the earlier plan; deficient monsoon in certain districts keeps management watchful.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "we expect slippages to trend materially downwards, in line with our guidance in the last quarter."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: R. Subramaniakumar

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Q2 fee growth of 12% includes a one-off; not repeatable
next_quarter_outlook.summary: A currency-swap related FCNR fee flattered sequential fee growth, so Q3 fee growth should not be extrapolated from Q2.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So, there is a one-off, which is why you see sequentially fee going up by 12%, right?"
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Bhavin Lakhpatwala

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Sequential loan growth of 5-6% a quarter suggested for modelling
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Executive Director clarifies how to translate the baseline into quarterly numbers.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "You might want to model a 6% or a 5% to 6% quarterly number."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Jaideep Iyer

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Opex growth to stay around 7-8% with a small uptick from branches, people and technology
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Collection-cost rationalisation in cards is largely done, so costs rise from here with branch, wealth and technology investment, but not materially.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "There may be a small uptick, with our investment in the branches go up and investment in the people goes up and technology, but it's not materially way away from what we have been showing."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: R. Subramaniakumar

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Branch expansion of 30-50 a quarter; 1,000 branches in about 2.5-3 years
next_quarter_outlook.summary: About 38 branches were due to open within two weeks; the earlier 1,000-branch ambition has stretched to 2.5-3 years.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "we are still committed to 1,000 branches in two years that we had called out earlier? ... Yes, around 2.5, 3 years, you can put it that way."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Param Subramanian (Investec); R. Subramaniakumar

next_quarter_outlook.topic: ENBD India business amalgamation to complete this financial year, subject to RBI approval
next_quarter_outlook.summary: The amalgamation application is with the RBI; management says completion is definitely in FY27 once approved.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "when does the ENBD India business acquisition get completed? ... Once the application is approved by them, thereafter, it will start. Definitely in this financial year."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Param Subramanian (Investec); R. Subramaniakumar

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Excess liquidity to be fully deployed in wholesale banking over the medium term
next_quarter_outlook.summary: After prepaying costly borrowings, remaining FCNR and capital-raise liquidity (about 35% of the May 2026 balance sheet) will take months to deploy and is aimed at better-rated corporates and secured retail.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Given the large liquidity still on the balance sheet, we expect to continue this for the next few months. Over the medium term, we expect this liquidity to be fully deployed in the wholesale banking segment"
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: R. Subramaniakumar

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Bancassurance fee income could fall 50-60% if the draft IRDAI circular is implemented as written
next_quarter_outlook.summary: About INR 300 cr of annual bancassurance income (about 8% of FY26 fees) is at risk; management says to pencil in a minimum 50-60% hit on a plain reading.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "I would imagine anywhere between 50% to 60% impact should be minimum to be penciled in."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Jaideep Iyer

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Loan growth baseline of 22-25% continues; model 5-6% per quarter
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Q2's 42% YoY (leverage- and liquidity-aided) is an exception; management treats 22-25% as the minimum baseline and suggests 5-6% sequential growth.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "You just look back in March and June, we said the baseline of between 22% to 25%. So, that baseline will be continued as we move forward. That's the minimum."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: R. Subramaniakumar

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Cards to return to growth in six months, then 10-12% next year
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Credit-card balances are still shrinking; the festive quarter should stop de-growth, with 10-12% growth expected next year and unsecured share staying near 19-20%.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "cards, we expect to start seeing at least some positive growth in the next six months before we start delivering a 10% to 12% growth for next year."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Jaideep Iyer

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Next-year mix: overall growth early-to-mid 20s, unsecured high single to low double digits
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Unsecured share of the book is expected to stay roughly where it is (19-20%, slightly lower).
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So, you can look at an overall growth of, let's say, early to mid-20s, and an unsecured growth of, let's say, high single digits or low double digits."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Jaideep Iyer

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Strategy and targets to be detailed over the coming months; no FY28 ROA guidance
next_quarter_outlook.summary: CEO declines FY28 ROA targets, asks investors to focus on the current 0.92% ROA, and promises full details over a few months; this is a catalyst for medium-term targets.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "I did say that over a period of next few months, we'll come back to you with a complete details."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: R. Subramaniakumar

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Tailwinds to margins and growth from fixed-rate liquidity in a rising-rate cycle
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Equity and FCNR funding that is effectively fixed-rate while lending rates rise gives a margin and growth tailwind, with cards and microfinance credit costs normalising.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So, there will be tailwind to margins. There is tailwind to growth."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Jaideep Iyer

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Liability costs to fall gradually; SA rates gradual, TD rates relative to market
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Deposit cost rationalisation continues but term-deposit rate cuts are tied to the market rate cycle.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "SA we would be a gradual. TD rates, I think I would caveat that by saying that will obviously be a function of economic interest rates."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Jaideep Iyer

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Wealth proposition at a very early stage
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Product, proposition and relationship managers will take time to build; no near-term launch.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So, don't expect something to be launched next week."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Bank management (speaker not named in transcript)

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Normalised LCR target 120-125% versus 148% now
next_quarter_outlook.summary: As excess liquidity is deployed, LCR will fall toward 120-125%, implying roughly 20+ points of liquidity release into earning assets.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Normally, we would want to be in the 120 to 125 zone on LCR, because there'll always be some cushion that we will want to keep."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Jaideep Iyer

analyst_focus.topic: How will NIM move in Q3 and Q4 as FCNR leverage and liquidity deployment play out?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Q2 NIM jumped 48 bps to 4.61% because surplus FCNR and equity liquidity sat in investments; five analysts asked for the path, the incremental yield on deployment, the full-quarter FCNR leverage cost and the repo-hike benefit. Answer: slightly lower in Q3, up in Q4, pace tied to deployment.

analyst_focus.topic: How badly will the draft IRDAI bancassurance rules hit fees?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Bancassurance is about INR 300 cr of income (8% of FY26 fees); management said to assume at least a 50-60% hit if implemented as drafted.

analyst_focus.topic: When do credit-card slippages and credit costs normalise?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Credit cost was INR 771 cr (63 bps) with cards provisioning of about INR 575 cr; analysts quantified the potential INR 175-250 cr saving. Management guided slippages to about 400 for Q3-Q4 and card credit cost to about 6%.

analyst_focus.topic: Can the retail deposit franchise improve CASA and reduce cost of funds?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Average CASA ratio was 24% (28.1% ex-FCNR) with flat average CASA and low single-digit SA growth; analysts asked whether balance sheet growth depends on SA growth and about branches, people, NRI and affluent initiatives.

analyst_focus.topic: What is the sustainable loan growth after a 42% YoY quarter?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts asked about FY27 and FY28 growth; management said the 22-25% baseline is the minimum and suggested 5-6% per quarter.

analyst_focus.topic: What ROA and targets for FY28 and beyond?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: With ROA at 0.92%, analysts proposed that lower credit cost could lift ROA toward 1.5% and asked about Board targets; management deferred specifics to coming months.

analyst_focus.topic: What is the wholesale lending strategy and its returns?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Wholesale advances grew 56% YoY; analysts asked about target ROA, sectors, short-term lending share and project finance; management emphasised risk- and capital-adjusted returns, working-capital and trade focus, and no single sector theme.

analyst_focus.topic: What happens to opex and branch rollout?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Opex grew only 3% YoY and 7% QoQ after collection-cost cuts; analysts asked if a normalised 7-8% growth is right and whether the 1,000-branch plan holds (now 2.5-3 years).

analyst_focus.topic: What will the unsecured and microfinance mix look like?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Unsecured assets grew only 11% YoY with yields of about 21% versus 9-10% for secured retail; analysts tested the margin drag from mix shift.

analyst_focus.topic: ENBD India amalgamation and wealth plans
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: The Emirates NBD group tie-up and wealth proposition drive medium-term franchise changes; management said the amalgamation is with the RBI and completes this fiscal year; wealth is early.

analyst_focus.topic: Liquidity buffers, duration and AFS marks
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: With LCR at 148% and rising yields, analysts asked about the target LCR (120-125%), MTM risk (management stayed short duration) and the AFS reserve.

analyst_focus.topic: Quality of fee growth and one-offs
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Core fee grew 12% YoY but retail fee only 9%; management confirmed an FCNR currency-swap related one-off lifted sequential growth.

analyst_focus.topic: ECL transition and steady-state credit cost
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Piran Engineer asked how ECL changes steady-state credit costs; management said mix drives it and declined a number.

key_risks: NIM is expected to dip in Q3 before improving; outcome depends on how fast liquidity is deployed into higher-yielding loans.
Draft IRDAI bancassurance rules could cut roughly INR 300 cr of annual fee income by at least 50-60%.
Deficient monsoon in certain districts keeps rural collections a watch item, though no stress has been seen so far.
Credit-card recovery is the main credit-cost lever; slippages must fall to the guided level.
Q2 growth and NIM include one-offs (FCNR leverage, swap-related fees) that will not repeat.
ENBD India amalgamation needs RBI approval, and medium-term targets have not yet been disclosed.
